questions.prompt: What is the absolute maximum value of f(x)=x³−3x on [−2,3]?
questions.explanation: The derivative is 3(x²−1), so the interior critical inputs are −1 and 1. Compare f(−2)=−2, f(−1)=2, f(1)=−2 and f(3)=18. The largest candidate value is 18, attained at endpoint 3. A: This is the local maximum at x=−1, not the absolute maximum on the whole interval. B: The endpoint x=3 has value 18, larger than every other endpoint or critical value. C: This is the attained minimum value, not the maximum. D: This is an input coordinate rather than the requested function value.

questions.prompt: At which input does f(x)=x⁴−8x² attain its absolute minimum on [−1,3]?
questions.explanation: The derivative factors as 4x(x²−4). Of its roots −2,0,2, only 0 and 2 are inside the interval. Candidate values are f(−1)=−7, f(0)=0, f(2)=−16 and f(3)=9. Hence the absolute minimum occurs at x=2. A: This derivative root lies outside the interval. B: The value there is 0, larger than −16. C: It has the smallest candidate value −16 among the allowed endpoints and critical inputs. D: The endpoint value is 9, not the minimum.

questions.prompt: What is the absolute minimum value of f(x)=|x−1| on [−2,2]?
questions.explanation: The function is continuous on the closed interval. Its nondifferentiable interior input 1 must be included as a critical candidate. Values at −2,1,2 are 3,0,1, so the minimum is 0 at x=1. A: This is the right endpoint value rather than the minimum. B: This is the left endpoint value and is the maximum. C: A derivative failure at the corner does not prevent an attained extremum. D: The continuous corner at x=1 is a candidate and attains zero.

questions.prompt: What is the absolute maximum value of f(x)=√(4−x²) on [−2,1]?
questions.explanation: The function is continuous on [−2,1]. Its interior derivative is −x/√(4−x²), zero only at 0. Include the endpoints even though the derivative at −2 is not finite. Values are 0,2,√3, so the absolute maximum value is 2. A: The interior critical input 0 has value 2. B: This is the right endpoint value, below 2. C: This is the left endpoint value. D: This is the maximum radicand, not its square root.

questions.prompt: At which input does f(x)=x e^(−x) attain its absolute maximum on [0,3]?
questions.explanation: The product and chain rules give f′=e^(−x)(1−x). Thus the only interior critical input is 1. Candidate values are 0,1/e,3/e³. Since e²>3, the middle value is larger than the right endpoint, so the maximum occurs at 1. A: The endpoint value is zero. B: The interior critical value 1/e exceeds both endpoint values. C: The endpoint value 3/e³ is smaller than 1/e. D: The derivative is negative and nonzero there.

questions.prompt: A continuous function on [a,b] has only finitely many interior critical points. Which procedure correctly finds its absolute extrema?
options: Compare only the derivative values at critical inputs.
Use only interior points where f′=0.
Evaluate f at both endpoints and every interior critical input, then compare those function values.
Choose the largest critical input for the maximum and the smallest for the minimum.
questions.explanation: The Candidates Test compares the original function values at endpoints and all interior critical points where the derivative is zero or fails to exist. Continuity on the closed interval guarantees absolute extrema, and this candidate list includes their possible locations. A: Extremal heights are values of f, not values of f′. B: This misses endpoints and nondifferentiable critical points. C: The candidate set includes endpoints, zero derivatives and derivative failures at defined interior points. D: Input order does not determine output order.

questions.prompt: The table below lists every candidate for a continuous function on [−1,5]. Where is its absolute minimum attained?
questions.explanation: Because the table is explicitly complete for all endpoints and interior critical inputs, compare its original function values. The smallest is −4, appearing at both 1 and 3. An absolute minimum value need not have a unique attaining input. A: The same least value also occurs at 3. B: The equal least value at 1 cannot be discarded. C: That candidate attains the greatest, not least, listed value. D: The least candidate value is −4 and both inputs attain it.

questions.prompt: What is the absolute maximum value of f(x)=x+4/x on [1,5]?
questions.explanation: On this positive interval, f′=1−4/x² vanishes only at 2. Evaluate f(1)=5, f(2)=4 and f(5)=29/5. Their largest value is 29/5, so the absolute maximum occurs at the right endpoint. A: The right endpoint value 5+4/5 exceeds the other candidate values 5 and 4. B: This is the interior minimum at x=2. C: This is the left endpoint value, smaller than 29/5. D: This is a critical input rather than a function height.

questions.prompt: At which input does f(x)=ln x−x attain its absolute minimum on [1/2,2]? A calculator may be used to compare values.
questions.explanation: The derivative 1/x−1 is zero only at 1. Values at the candidates 1/2,1,2 are −ln2−1/2≈−1.1931, −1 and ln2−2≈−1.3069. The least is at x=2. All candidates lie in the positive logarithm domain. A: This endpoint value is higher than the value at 2. B: The candidate values are approximately −1.1931, −1 and −1.3069, with the last smallest. C: The interior critical input gives the maximum among the candidates. D: This input is outside both the interval and the logarithm domain.

questions.prompt: For f(x)=x² on the open interval (−1,1), which statement about the Candidates Test is correct?
options: The maximum is 1 at x=−1 and x=1.
The minimum and maximum both occur at the only critical input 0.
The minimum is 0 at x=0, but no absolute maximum is attained because the bounding endpoints are absent.
No minimum exists because the interval is open.
questions.explanation: The value zero is attained at the interior critical input 0 and is the minimum by x²≥0. Every domain output is less than 1, with values arbitrarily close to 1 near the excluded endpoints. Thus no maximum is attained and a closed-interval endpoint comparison cannot be copied blindly. A: Those inputs are not in the domain. B: A single critical input does not force the same point to be both extrema. C: The critical point attains the minimum, while the supremum 1 is only approached. D: Openness removes a general guarantee, not every actual extremum.

questions.prompt: A student finds the only interior critical input x=0 for f(x)=x² on [−1,2] and claims the absolute maximum is f(0)=0. Which correction is valid?
options: The student is correct because only derivative zeros matter.
The maximum is 1 because the left endpoint is listed first.
There is no maximum because f′(2)≠0.
Include endpoints: f(−1)=1 and f(2)=4, so the absolute maximum is 4 at x=2.
questions.explanation: The closed-interval test must include −1 and 2 as well as interior critical input 0. The three function values are 1,0,4, so the largest is 4 at x=2. No endpoint stationarity condition is required. A: Closed-interval absolute extrema can occur at endpoints. B: The right endpoint has the larger value 4. C: An endpoint maximum need not have a zero derivative. D: The student omitted endpoint candidates and mistook an interior minimum for a maximum.
